recipes.name: Pop’s Dill Pickles
ingredients_raw: 3 tablespoons pickling spice, wrapped in cheesecloth
7 1-quart canning jars with lids and rings

steps.text: Place cucumbers in a large pot and cover with ice cubes. Let sit for at least 2 hours and up to 8 hours. Drain and pat dry.
Place water, vinegar, sugar, pickling salt, and pickling spice into a large saucepan. Bring to a boil; simmer pickling liquid for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, sterilize the jars and lids in a large pot of boiling water for at least 5 minutes. Pack cucumbers into the hot, sterilized jars, filling the jars to within 1/2 inch of the top. Place 1 dill head and 1 garlic clove into each jar.
Pour hot pickling liquid into the jars, filling to within 1/4 inch of the rim. Wipe the jar rims with a moist paper towel to remove any food residue. Top with the lids and screw on the rings.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then carefully lower the jars into the pot using a holder. Leave a 2-inch space between the jars. Pour in more boiling water if necessary until the water level is at least 1 inch above the tops of the jars. Bring water to a full boil, cover the pot, and process for 5 minutes.

Remove the jars from the stockpot and place onto a cloth-covered or wood surface, several inches apart, until cool. Once cool, press down on the top of each lid, ensuring the seal is tight (lid should not move up or down at all). If any the jars aren’t sealed properly, refrigerate them and eat within two weeks.
Store the sealed jars in a cool, dark area. Wait for at least 1 week before opening.

raw_recipe.headline: Pop’s Dill Pickles
raw_recipe.description: This delicious dill pickle recipe packs crunchy cucumbers into jars with a sweet and tangy pickling brine flavored with fresh dill, garlic, and spices.

review.reviewBody: No one needs to add any chemicals or pickle crisp in their pickles. When washing your cucumbers cut the flower end off of it. There is an enzyme in it that will eventually cause your pickles to go soft. Everyone raves over mine and I haven't had a jar of pickles go soft for years even after being in the jar for a year.

Good Basic Recipe for pickles. I made this by cutting my cucumbers into spears and cutting the blossom end off. I could not locate fresh dill heads and did not want the little pieces of green on the pickle, so I used dill seed. What I liked about this recipe is the right balance of salt and sweet, the sterilization instructions, and the amount of processing time, and the fact that you can adapt this recipe to your tastes by adding garlic or hot peppers. I did add 1/4 tsp of pickling crisp to each of my quart jars based upon advice from other Canners. I used two tsps of dill seed per jar and added half of a seeded serrano pepper to two of the 4 jars. My daughter is intrigued by the process so I am going back to the farmer's market for more cucumbers. Thanks for sharing a great recipe that takes me down memory lane.

UPDATE
After 8 wks, we opened a jar and they were delicious. The pickles are crunchy and the taste of the dill, garlic, salt, vinegar, and sugar are perfect.

I found this recipe a little bit too sweet and too much "spice" from the pickling spice. I changed the sugar to 1/2 cup and removed the step to boil the brine with the sachet of spice. Instead, in each jar I added 1/8 tsp. of pickling spice right in the jar. I let it sit for a min of 4 days, and it was great!

So...
4C. Water
4C. Vinegar
1/2C. Sugar
1/2C. Pickling Salt
-Bring to boil and simmer for 10 min

In each jar add fresh dill, garlic and pickling spice. Happy Pickling!

I made it the first time as listed but didn't like the sweetness from the sugar so omitted it the second time. Also added the pickling spice directly to the jars along with extra bay leaves and 2 whole cloves & chopped garlic. Used "pickle crisp" and grape leaves to keep the crunchy texture. They are being devoured! I used the same brine to make spicy pickled beans for Caesars and added some chili flakes. Such a great way to preserve the abundance growing in my garden!

Excellent recipe! Although I love garlic, I prefer the simpler taste of "Pop's" original recipe without garlic. The first time I made these, I didn't have dill heads or seed, so I substituted 4 sprigs of fresh dill weed per 1 litre jar (2 sprigs at the bottom, 2 sprigs on top), and the result was great. I find have to increase the brine recipe by about a half to make sure I can fully cover the pickles.

This is a really nice and adaptable pickle recipe. I had 14 3-4 pickling cukes from a friend and ended up with 4 pints of spears and two pints of chips. I used my v-slicer to cut the chips. I didn't bother with the cheesecloth because I like the way it looks to have the spices floating in the jar. I only used 1/4 cup of sugar because we don't really like sweet pickles, and I added a sprinkle of red pepper flakes for fun. I just used kosher salt because that's what I had. Next time I'm going to pop a few grape leaves in the jars too. The pickles are delicious, and it was fun to experiment with canning.

Perfect with adjustment.
Firstly, only add all the sugar if you like sweet pickles. I like my pickles less sweet so I only added 2 tbsp of sugar.
Next, this is not enough brine to make 7 quarts. I made another half of the brine to fill the rest of jars.
Last, make sure you don't can the pickles with the pickling spice(I didn't have cheesecloth so I just strained the brine) or it will over power the pickles.

I followed the recipe exactly, found like several others that I did not have enough liquid. That wasn’t a tragedy—I made more. The problem for me is that the pickles are waaaay too salty! I also didn’t understand the instructions to cover the cucumbers with ice. Why? The ones on top obviously get much more exposure to the ice than those on the bottom. Maybe ice water would be better? Other than that, they were reasonably easy to do and I liked that the recipe could be scaled. I suggest packing your cucumbers into the jars ahead of time so that you know how many jars you’ll need. In my opinion, the jars don’t need to be pre-boiled—dish washer and keep them hot should be sufficient, but check with your extension office on this. Also, scrub and trim the blossom end before the ice treatment.

Finally! An easy and tasty recipe! These pickles were amazing! After reading reviews I made 50% more brine and had a little leftover. One clove of garlic and 1-2 dill heads was the perfect balance. I added a Thai chili pepper to a few jars for fun and the spice was just perfect. 

I didn't soak my cukes - just took them from the fridge and they were great.

They tasted great after a month on the shelf but I popped a few jars into the fridge without processing and they were DIVINE after a week.

I just tried this recipe, my first attempt at making pickles . The directions were easy to follow. I read many reviews and I will agree, double the brine for the quart jars. I was able to fill 7 quarts. I didnt have dill heads so I used a few dill sprigs in each jar. I added a few more garlic cloves to a few jars for an extra kick.They smelled good and I'm hoping in a week they taste just as good.

I did not have enough brine, I even added more to the receipe...I thought I packed the jars tight 
Added the garlic, peppercorns and a few red Thai chilies in a couple, I like them zesty!
I made it as is and thought it was great and so did my family.
This has been a family favorite. I've brought them to church fundraisers and they go fast.
I’ve made these in the past and it is my go to recipe every year. Can hardly wait to crack a jar!
So far from what I can tell supper easy to make. But now is the hardest part the wait to try them. And this family loves their pickels.

I don’t even care for dill pickles but this one changed my mind! I followed the recipe but reduced the sugar to a scant 1/2 C as well as less salt (1/3 C). The game changer was also to stuff the jar with extra garlic cloves and fresh dill heads. Wonderful recipe & easy to follow. Thank you for sharing it! 💕
What more can I say! This is an easy and tasty recipe! My family loves the pickles.

I double this and make half the jars with garlic and half without. Handy to have in the pantry when visiting friends at their cabin, my kids take some home and we all just love them. Making them for years! I think they are now Deb’s Pickles haha.

My family devoured these! Use fresh dill. Soak the cukes in ice water for a few hours. These are great tasting, they really have a strong flavor....I always use extra dill and an extra clove of garlic per quart.

You will need to remove bubbles placing butter knife down sides for this purpose. Also great grandma always put Cherry tree leaves in each jar. This ensures the crunch My pickles are requested they are so good.
